Authored treated-studio monitoring is not an assertion about actual performance acoustics. Broad bassSystem.ukSoundsystem reflects the positively documented dubstep/bass DJ branch, not a universal tempo or fixed bar structure.

Exact decks, media format and source studio palettes are unspecified. Cinematic Dubstep is the DubKraft-associated imaginative soundtrack strand, not a synonym for commissioned film score or an assumed orchestral layer. Label founder Alien Pimp’s own2009 announcement explicitly defines an imaginary-film emotional programme, spanning dancefloor and headphone listening and several bass-related styles. Existing dubstep/dubstep_140 cover the broader South London half-time/sub-bass field; minimal_dubstep foregrounds sparse production; classic_dubstep is a historical discovery umbrella rather than a strict year exclusion. Those overlap this field but do not define its positive soundtrack-oriented label/repertoire axis. Existing experimental_dubstep selects a broader live global-bass network, and cinematic_post_rock a guitar-based post-rock neighborhood. The selected complete guest mix includes adjacent electro/IDM/breakstep material: it is a documented DJ practice of a named compilation participant, not proof every track is exclusively cinematic dubstep. Historical creator observation includes Full Spektrum and Alien Pimp; current creator access fails, so label/issuer evidence is independently stated. All eleven credited people retained: Juanes lead voice/guitar; Felipe Navia bass; Juan Pablo Daza guitar; Richard Bravo percussion; Marcelo Novati drums; Miguel Ortiz trumpet; Felipe Silva tenor saxophone; Percy Recavarren trombone; Nicolle Horbath and Daniel Olivero voices; Emmanuel Briceño keyboards/musical direction. Two guitarists aggregate in one guitar-family card, three named singers in the live-group voice card. The eyewitness issuer also reports audience singalong in La Luz; additional participating audience voices have unknown count and are retained conceptually in the same group voice role, not falsely counted as only three audible humans. Neither production staff nor musical direction adds another sound-producing role. Representative authored realization of the fully credited ensemble. The source expressly identifies tenor saxophone and trumpet/trombone, retained as distinct cards. Broad functionalSong with pop family models an authored tonal popular-song realization; the merengue variant in one song does not reclassify the whole category as a dance genre.

Full existing bangla_pop is a broad Bengali popular-music field represented by Miles; its Dhaka example is not a categorical exclusion of West Bengal. West Bengali Pop is an overlapping narrower regional production and concert community spanning Kolkata/West Bengal film songs, bands and soloists. The exact creator includes Anupam Roy, Anjan Dutt, Chandrabindoo, Somlata and Arindom. Techno India University documents the Kolkata multi-college Sahotsava network with Anupam Roy, Fossils, Anjan Dutt and Underground Authority across years; SVF documents its Bengali film/music production infrastructure. This positive regional institutional axis is not a different piano arrangement or language-exclusive rule: regional artists also sing other languages. Existing Rabindra Sangeet and Nazrul Geeti denote bounded composer repertoires, while Bengali Baul/lokgeeti denote specific traditional practices; this current popular regional field overlaps performances of those repertoires but is not coextensive. Bangladeshi indie/rock/hiphop describe communities across the national border, not all Bengali language music. Senter’s own artist profile identifies Mass as founder and mentor of that network while candidly also representing Tamil, Hindi and Maldivian influences. Exact creator playlist includes Mass1/18/55/92, Jizzy2 and J!NNA6/59/94; a multilingual roster does not establish language purity. Existing sinhala_pop describes the national-language popular-song mainstream, with guitar-combo, baila and cassette histories; the documented electronic dance producer/label field is a narrower overlapping contemporary branch, not an assertion Sinhala Pop excludes electronics. Existing sinhala_rap addresses MC/sung-rap practice and may share collaborators; Sinhala Indie covers independent rock without exhausting independent electronic production. Other compilation tracks with bronze percussion, belikan and nature recordings are not part of this selected full track. tradition.name: Dansk Lovsang
tradition.lineage: Complete approximately one-hour Den Danske Salmeduo anniversary concert as announced by Sankt Lukas Kirke, Aarhus, for 20 September 2026: Christian Vuust doubles saxophone and clarinet; Hans Esbjerg plays piano. Two performers, three instrument families, zero singers in this explicitly instrumental hymn reinterpretation. This is the entire announced duo practice, not an extracted instrumental stem from a vocal song. Exact set list, saxophone register, instrument models and actual attendance are not documented; source announcement is not proof the event occurred. Authored intimate live-room rendition: standard studio upright piano with jazz-comping chords, yellow-brass tenor saxophone with medium reed/hard-rubber mouthpiece and Selmer Mark VI school, grenadilla A clarinet with medium reed and softly tongued legato phrasing. These are coherent editorial construction and technique choices for the source-unspecified instruments, not claims about Vuust or Esbjerg equipment. One reed player alternates the two cards rather than three simultaneous people. No global temperament or recording apparatus inferred. Broad ritualDevotional follows the Christian hymn repertoire; this instrumental concert branch does not assert congregational singing or Black-gospel technique.

tradition.lineage: Complete tamborilero instrumental practice explicitly described by Canal Extremadura on18September2026, particularly in Sierra de Gata: one performer simultaneously plays the three-hole gaita with one hand and tamboril with the other, maintaining melody and rhythm without voice. Two instrument cards, one person, zero singers. This is the documented practice, not the full radio programme or an invented isolated stem of the separately named Manantial Folk recordings.

Castilla y León and Navarre remain their own overlapping regional communities. Portuguese folk overlaps through the documented Olivenza border influence without exhausting Extremaduran practices. Galician gaita is a bagpipe and is not substituted for this three-hole duct pipe. No claim of strictly nonoverlapping sounds or national isolation. Authored ornamented melodic elaboration over the player’s own recurring tabor metric frame, placed under broad improvOnFrame in light of the practitioner’s explicitly documented live variations/ornaments. Regional duct pipe retains three holes, one-handed self-accompaniment and wooden body; pitch, exact bore and wood species unspecified. Existing tamboril regional form and all four drum controls retained. Calfskin slack heads with gut snare over struck head are authored physical choices, not source measurements. Controlled live-room rendition with no specific microphone/chain claim. The up-tempo tabor output is an explicitly authored brisk dance rendition within the documented dance/celebration practice, not a measured source BPM or a claim every regional ritual is fast.

tradition.lineage: Camilo Pajuelo — complete producer-issued2014 Helme solo-guitar film, adapted by Raúl García Zárate. The producer explicitly documents a continuous three-section instrumental drama: dialogue, tragedy and ayataki. One guitarist and one guitar retained, no singer or band inferred; literary characters and funeral-song origin do not constitute credited vocal roles. Producer confirms filmed Helsinki location and Andean-guitar identity. The exact composition is documented independently in research based on García Zárate testimony; its alternate-tuning practice is known, but exact strings/pitch standard of this2014 performance are not measured or asserted. Source-compatible authored six-string spruce/fan-braced nylon guitar with fingerpicked free-stroke attack, not source instrument make/material identification. Isolated owner preserves all six original meaningful control dimensions while replacing mandatory standard EADGBE with documented Andean variable tuning, exact tuning unknown. This is no arbitrary new timbre-only owner: physical string-tuning incompatibility requires a truthful slot. No existing instrument/shared part is edited. Broad artMusic reflects the expressly arranged continuous three-part instrumental narrative; no verse-chorus or improvisation invented. Spacious recital hall is an authored listening rendition, not original Helsinki building acoustics; optional chain and global temperament omitted.

Lalgudi violin lineage follows the actual featured violinist; Palghat mridangam lineage is positively supported by a first-person fellow musician’s account of Raghu studying with Mani Iyer. Microtonally inflected bowing, seated South Indian posture, tonic/fifth violin tuning and synthetic strings are explicit representative choices, not measured 1973 equipment. Mridangam jackwood/goat-buffalo construction and standard heads are authored. Ghatam Manamadurai denotes an authored clay-temper construction choice, not Vinayakram’s personal pedagogical lineage or identified historical pot; full-bowl strike is an authored default, not an assertion excluding other gestures. Controlled live room and neutral numeric axes are authored; global temperament and capture apparatus omitted. No new instrument owner or source-inferred lineage is introduced.

Senri Records explicitly credits the duo Yousei Suzuki and Haruyuki Umeki and describes the full source as improvisation with two acoustic guitars, accumulated during home gatherings over approximately five years. All sixteen pieces and both instrumental performers are included; one existing guitar-family card aggregates the two like instruments, not a claim of a solo performer. No separately credited singer. The issuer explicitly tags Japanese experimental music, avant-garde and primitive guitar; the Japanese text also states two acoustic guitars and improvisation. The actual existing japanoise row specifies maximal-density electronics and saturation; this positively self-described Japanese experimental acoustic improvisation practice demonstrates a broader experimental field rather than a renamed noise subgenre. Existing free_improvisation is a non-idiomatic European/American process tradition and overlaps this selected practice; the regional experimental discovery umbrella also crosses processes and is not asserted to invent a separate guitar technique. Parent improvOnFrame.jamFree explicitly includes loosely structured collective free improvisation and fits this complete release, without asserting every Japanese experimental piece is improvised. Contemporary all-mahogany steel-string dreadnought construction and flatpicked note articulation are a candid representative authored realization of unspecified acoustic guitars, not measured original models, strings or exact gestures. Controlled live-room capture is authored rather than a claim to reconstruct the actual homes.

tradition.name: Japanese worship
tradition.lineage: Takahiro Tone Nakamine — Ai No Iro, documented regular solo-acoustic performance practice. The artist’s self-written discography explicitly states that Ai No Iro is regularly performed at Tone’s solo acoustic shows. The official Heroes EP notes identify this particular work as an acoustic worship song in Japanese, and its complete published lyrics address Jesus and the cross. Select the complete documented solo-acoustic rendition practice: one singer accompanying himself on acoustic guitar. This is not an asserted transcription of the2013 studio master or an arbitrary stripping of the full band EP. Bass, drums and backing singers credited to other versions/full EP are not attributed to the explicitly solo performance. Japanese worship is a Japanese-language/local Christian devotional repertoire and community, overlapping global contemporary worship without being identical to its codified evangelical congregational rock-band practice. The artist documents ongoing church/community activity around Tokyo and Yokohama and explicitly identifies Japanese acoustic worship repertoire. Existing christian_rock traces an American evangelical/CCM rock industry; this named regional-language sacred field also contains a positively documented solo acoustic branch. No claim that American churches exclude acoustic music, or that one performer proves a unique national timbre. Broad ritualDevotional captures the actual praise/prayer function without assuming a Pentecostal denomination or metal sound from the artist’s broader identity. All-mahogany steel-string dreadnought construction and flatpicked note articulation are authored modern acoustic realization choices, not source guitar model or measured gestures. One real singer remains one voice with source-unspecified physiology and no invented choir. Controlled live-room acoustics and omitted apparatus/global tuning are authored rather than claimed session facts.

tradition.lineage: Michael Mawoni — complete Hiwumbe Awumba (God Creates And Then Destroys), Smithsonian SFW40504_103, 2:34, issued2003. The issuer explicitly credits the same sole musician with lead vocals and adungu; retain both roles and one singer. This is the whole separately issued Nyole-language track, not an arbitrary layer from the wider Abayudaya album. The chorus, guitars, keyboards and drums on other album tracks are outside this complete selection. Broad ritualDevotional is scoped to this sacred song contemplating God and mortality, supported by the issuer sacred classification and collector transcription; it does not classify every Ugandan tradition as religious. Authored alto-register adungu with nylon strings/hide resonator and gentle devotional accompaniment. The existing church/liturgical setting is used for its nonsectarian devotional descriptors, not a claim of Christian worship. Alur in the instrument name describes its catalog instrument lineage, not the Nyole singer ethnicity. Exact harp size/string material are proposed physical defaults, not measured source facts. All17 original voice controls retained: one accompanied sung voice, source-unspecified physiology, neutral effort/tract, unprocessed single lead. No measured temperament, capture apparatus or extra singers invented. Spacious acoustic shoebox-hall listening setting is a proposed new rendition, not field-recording metadata.
